Your first launch

Ride the sky.

A tow. A release. Then the quietest view in Western New York.

ChooseWhat to expectPrepareRequest

Not a simulation

This is real soaring.

Climb behind a towplane, release over the Genesee Valley, and discover what a sailplane can do with nothing but altitude, air, and a pilot who knows how to use both.

Flights depend on weather, field conditions, aircraft, tow capability, and qualified volunteer availability. A request is not confirmed until the club responds.

The sequence

From briefing to touchdown.

01

Check in

Meet the field team, complete required paperwork, and review the day’s conditions.

02

Fit & brief

Learn cockpit entry, restraint, controls to avoid, signals, and what to expect on tow.

03

Launch

The towplane accelerates the glider and climbs to the selected release altitude.

04

Soar

After release, take in the quiet, the view, and how efficiently the aircraft moves.

05

Land & debrief

Return through a planned pattern, touch down, then ask every question you collected aloft.

Wear

Closed-toe shoes, flexible layers, sunglasses, and sun protection.

Bring

Water, schedule flexibility, and details about fit or mobility needs.

Leave secured

Loose objects can become hazards. Ask before using a camera or mount.

Request a flight

Your seat is waiting.

Send the volunteer ride team your preferred dates and experience choice. Your email app will open with the request prepared; this page does not store your information.

  • Confirmation follows by email or phone
  • One passenger per glider flight
  • Ask about fit, mobility, or age considerations

No data is stored on this site. Submitting opens your email application.
